The von Mises stress in the tank floor initially increases during the first 15 minutes of operation due to the rising salt inventory temperature, as seen in Figures 12 and 13. After this initial period, stress levels begin to fluctuate as the incoming salt mixes better with the existing inventory. The analysis clearly shows that stress increases with tank diameter, suggesting that smaller tanks are better suited to achieving lower operational stress. Conversely, thickening the floor resulted in only a significant reduction in the peak stress when the floor was increased from 7 mm to 14 mm, but only a slight stress reduction when increased to 21 mm, indicating a non-linear relationship between the stresses and floor thickness. In general, there are low operation stresses produced using a flat floor model without initial residual stress, suggesting that the impact of the floor thickness and tank diameter should be assessed when welding-induced residual stress and distortion are incorporated into the analysis. a) a) b) b) c) c) Figure 12.
